categories.absence: something the archive does not contain; the right answer is silence
categories.constraint: a limit that constrains an otherwise plausible action
categories.current_fact: what is true now about one named thing
categories.historical: what was true before, and what replaced it
categories.multi_topic: a question spanning two documented areas
categories.near_miss: a question that sounds answerable and is not, at the vocabulary boundary
categories.scope_confusion: two similarly named things; the answer is the one that was asked for
categories.why_decision: the reasoning behind a choice, asked indirectly

spec.name: held-out v3
rules: A question is answerable unless expect_state is ABSENT.
For an ABSENT question the only correct behaviour is to return nothing.
A question answered from the wrong document is wrong, not abstention.
Paraphrase, do not quote: the source sentence must not appear verbatim in the question.
The scoring rubric is four outcomes, not an accuracy: correct, abstained when answerable, answered wrong, answered when it should have abstained.
spec.scoring: exactly once, at one commit, by a scorer that has not seen retrieval code
spec.source_of_questions: the ten maintainer questions from the first-hour audit, plus the question shapes the measured failure classes predict
spec.why_v3: held-out v2 already exists (32 questions, frozen 2026-10-04, already scored). A second set under that name would make the identifier ambiguous.
